name: Battle of Grunwald
summary: On July 15, 1410, the combined Polish-Lithuanian army under Władysław II Jagiełło (Poland) and Vytautas (Lithuania) confronts the Teutonic Order's army under Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen at Grunwald (Tannenberg). The 50,000+ Polish-Lithuanian force faces 27,000 Teutonic knights. The Grand Master and most senior officers are killed; the Teutonic Order's military power is permanently broken. The battle is the largest pitched battle in medieval European history to that point and establishes Poland-Lithuania as the dominant power in central-eastern Europe.

_quarry.structural_significance: Permanently ends Teutonic Order offensive military capability; establishes Polish-Lithuanian supremacy in the Baltic region; demonstrates that combined-arms professional armies could defeat the most formidable crusading military order
